derivations.claim: Apply [F3] to each level-$r$ rectangle. Its proof counts fault-witness sets and uses only the local-stochastic subset bound, so it requires no independence between child fault indicators. Thus each top-level circuit rectangle is bad with probability at most $p_r=A^{-1/q}(A^{1/q}\eta)^{(q+1)^r}$.

If $\eta=0$, each single-location fault event has probability zero by the local-stochastic subset bound; the finite union bound gives no faults almost surely, so level zero suffices. Otherwise put $\theta=A^{1/q}\eta\in(0,1)$ and $c=-\log\theta>0$. Any $r$ with $(q+1)^r\ge c^{-1}\log(NA^{-1/q}/\delta)$ is sufficient; if the logarithm is nonpositive or its positive value is at most $c$, $r=0$ suffices. For fixed parameters, the least qualifying $r$ is $O(\log\log(N/\delta))$ as $N/\delta\to\infty$.

By [F11], the probability $\alpha$ that at least one of the $N$ top-level circuit rectangles is bad satisfies $\alpha\le Np_r$. For every fault pattern, [F9] gives a conditional channel, so its output on the fixed input and reference is a density operator. On the complementary event, recursive goodness gives at most $q$ bad children in every stage. The contract [F8] and sparse-path correction guarantee [F4] make each corrected logical stage ideal for the per-location channels allowed by [F1]. Thus every pattern with no bad top-level rectangle outputs $\rho_{\mathrm{id}}$. If $\alpha>0$, the normalized finite mixture of bad-pattern outputs is a density operator $\tau$; if $\alpha=0$, choose any density operator for $\tau$. Then $\rho_{\mathrm{out}}=(1-\alpha)\rho_{\mathrm{id}}+\alpha\tau$, and [F10] confirms that the weighted schedule output is a channel.

By homogeneity of trace distance and [F6], $D(\rho_{\mathrm{out}},\rho_{\mathrm{id}})=\alpha D(\tau,\rho_{\mathrm{id}})\le\alpha\le Np_r$. Applying [F7] to the final POVM bounds its output total-variation distance by $Np_r$, and every success event changes by at most that total-variation distance.

Because the gadget family is fixed and finite, some constant $\kappa\ge1$ bounds size and depth expansion at every replacement level. Thus total size and depth are at most $C\kappa^r$ for a fixed $C$, which is polylogarithmic in $N/\delta$ by step 1.2.

derivations.claim: Since $q=\lfloor d/(2\ell)\rfloor$, we have $2q\ell\le d$. Also $A\ge1$, and $A\eta^q<1$ gives $\theta:=A^{1/q}\eta<1$. Apply [F2] to obtain $p_r\le A^{-1/q}\theta^{(q+1)^r}$.

If $\eta=0$, the product fault law gives probability zero to every nonempty fault pattern, so $p_0=0$ and level zero suffices. If $\eta>0$, put $c=-\log\theta>0$. Any $r$ with $(q+1)^r\ge c^{-1}\log(NA^{-1/q}/\delta)$ gives $Np_r\le\delta$ by [F2]; if the logarithm is nonpositive or its positive value is at most $c$, level $r=0$ suffices. For fixed $A,q,\eta$ with $0<\theta<1$, the least qualifying level is $O(\log\log(N/\delta))$ as $N/\delta\to\infty$.

The event that any of the $N$ top-level circuit rectangles is bad is the union of $N$ events, each of probability at most $p_r$. The finite union bound [F8] gives $\alpha:=\mathbb P(\text{some top-level rectangle is bad})\le Np_r$.

For every fault pattern, [F9] gives a conditional channel, so its output on the fixed input and reference is a density operator. On the event that all top-level rectangles are $q$-good, recursive goodness gives at most $q$ bad children in each computation and correction stage. The gadget contracts [F7] and sparse-path induction [F3] then make every corrected stage ideal, so every such pattern outputs $\rho_{\mathrm{id}}$. If $\alpha>0$, the normalized finite mixture of outputs from bad patterns is a density operator $\tau$; if $\alpha=0$, choose any density operator for $\tau$. Thus $\rho_{\mathrm{out}}=(1-\alpha)\rho_{\mathrm{id}}+\alpha\tau$, and [F10] confirms that this weighted schedule output is a channel.

By homogeneity of the trace norm, $D(\rho_{\mathrm{out}},\rho_{\mathrm{id}})=\alpha D(\tau,\rho_{\mathrm{id}})\le\alpha\le Np_r$, where the first inequality is [F5]. The same identity holds after tensoring any reference identity, since the gadget contracts preserve the reference.

Apply [F6] to the final finite POVM. Its output total-variation distance is at most $D(\rho_{\mathrm{out}},\rho_{\mathrm{id}})\le Np_r$. For any success event $E$, $|P_{\mathrm{out}}(E)-P_{\mathrm{id}}(E)|\le \tfrac12\sum_x|P_{\mathrm{out}}(x)-P_{\mathrm{id}}(x)|$, so the success-probability change is at most $Np_r$.

Because the gadget family is fixed and finite, some constant $\kappa\ge1$ bounds size and depth expansion at every replacement level. Thus total size and depth are at most $C\kappa^r$ for a fixed $C$. Since $r=O(\log\log(N/\delta))$, this is a fixed power of $\log(N/\delta)$, hence the overhead is polylogarithmic.
